about.title: About
about.tagline: The first international gathering around Vodun arts, culture, and spirituality.
about.description: From January 8 to 10, 2026, Ouidah becomes the international capital of Vodun celebration. Hounve dances, Zangbeto and Egungun processions, ceremonies honoring the deities, open-air concerts by the sea...
about.place: Gate of No Return, Ouidah Beach

help.title: Help & Support
help.subtitle: Frequently asked questions about Vodun Days 2026.

faq.q: What are the dates of Vodun Days?
faq.a: Vodun Days take place on January 8, 9, and 10, 2026 in Ouidah, near the Gate of No Return.

faq.q: How to get to Ouidah from Cotonou?
faq.a: Ouidah is about 40 km from Cotonou, approximately 1 hour by car. You can use your own vehicle or a ride-hailing service.

faq.q: Do I need a visa to visit Benin?
faq.a: Benin offers an e-Visa within a few hours at evisa.bj. Fees: 50 EUR (30-day single), 75 EUR (30-day multiple), 100 EUR (90-day multiple).
Cotonou's Bernardin Gantin Airport, located about 40 km from Ouidah, is recommended for international participants.
Yes! The camping area is close to the Arena, the stage, and the beach. 7,000 FCFA/night with your own tent, 20,000 FCFA/night with a rented tent.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.sessionDesc: Your session is identified by a temporary UUID, randomly generated. It is deleted when the app closes and cannot identify you.
privacy.legalNote: Privacy policy of Benin Tourisme, organizer of Vodun Days. Based on article 415 of the Digital Code of the Republic of Benin.

sections.title: No personal data retained
sections.content: This application does not collect, store, or transmit any personal data. Your identity remains completely anonymous.

sections.title: Session UUID identification
sections.content: The app uses a randomly generated UUID for each session. This identifier is temporary, non-nominal, and automatically deleted when the application closes. It cannot identify you.

sections.title: Data collected on the website
sections.content: The policy below concerns the site vodundays.bj. Benin Tourisme may collect name, first name, and contact information (email, phone) only if you fill out a form.

sections.title: Purpose of processing (website)
sections.content: Website data is used for marketing, promotions, and complaint management, in compliance with the Digital Code of the Republic of Benin.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.content: You have the right to access, rectify, erase, limit, port, and object to your data. Contact contact@vodundays.bj to exercise your rights.

pedagogie.intro: Vodun Days celebrate January 10, Benin's national Vodun holiday. This celebration honors the deities and ancestors through millennia-old rituals, processions, and ceremonies, heirs to the traditions of the Slave Coast.

placeMaro.name: Place Maro
placeMaro.description: Place Maro is an iconic location in Ouidah where Egungun ceremonies take place. These ancestral masks represent the spirits of ancestors returned to guide and bless the living through millennia-old rituals.

esplanade.name: Esplanade du Fort Français
esplanade.description: The Esplanade du Fort Français hosts the Zangbeto ceremonies, nocturnal guardians of the Yoruba tradition. The Brazilian Terreiros bear witness to the historical ties between Benin and Brazil through the diaspora.

placeNinsouxwe.name: Place Ninsouxwe
placeNinsouxwe.description: A sacred place dedicated to the deities Zomadonou and Ninsouxwe, protectors of the city. The ceremonies held here perpetuate ancestral traditions passed down from generation to generation.

foretSacree.name: Sacred Forest of Kpasse
foretSacree.description: The Sacred Forest of Kpasse is home to the deities Thron, Hounve, Kabada, and Koku. This natural sanctuary is a place of contemplation and communion with the spiritual forces of nature and the ancestors.

templeMami.name: Temple Mami Plage
templeMami.description: Temple Mami Plage is dedicated to Mami Wata, the goddess of the waters. The ceremonies honor this powerful deity who reigns over the oceans and brings prosperity to those who venerate her.

couventSakpata.name: Couvent Sakpata
couventSakpata.description: The Couvent Sakpata is dedicated to the vodun of earth and smallpox. Sakpata is a feared and respected deity, guarantor of divine justice and the balance between the visible and invisible worlds.

hero.title: Celebrate the Tradition
hero.subtitle: Three days where Ouidah awakens to the rhythm of drums. Rituals, sacred dances and ancestral traditions, the living soul of Benin.

about.para1: Vodun Days celebrate the traditional religion of Benin. Every year on January 10th, Ouidah becomes the world center of Vodun spirituality.
about.para2: Discover sacred ceremonies, ritual dances, and traditional crafts in an atmosphere of communion and cultural sharing unique in the world.
